name: How do built-in appliances differ from freestanding in terms of kitchen layout?

mainEntity.name: How do built-in appliances differ from freestanding in terms of kitchen layout?

acceptedAnswer.text: Built-in appliances, such as integrated refrigerators, wall ovens, and cooktops, require custom cabinetry and precise cutouts for a seamless, flush appearance. They often offer a more streamlined aesthetic and save counter space. Freestanding appliances, like traditional ranges and refrigerators, are typically easier to install and can be moved. The choice impacts the kitchen layout significantly: built-ins demand meticulous planning of cabinet dimensions and utility placement, while freestanding appliances allow for more flexibility in a layout but may interrupt continuous lines.
acceptedAnswer.description: Built-in appliances need custom cabinetry and precise planning for a seamless look, while freestanding options are more flexible but can interrupt design lines.
